title: Battered Cod and Oven Chips
subtitle: Crispy battered cod with chunky baked chips
excerpt: A lighter take on fish and chips that bakes the potatoes and shallow-fries the battered cod in a good layer of hot oil. Self-raising flour gives the batter its lift. The result is crisp, golden fish with fluffy oven chips and none of the deep-fat fryer required.
sourceNotes: Fish and chips became a staple British takeaway from the 1860s. The combination of battered fish and fried potatoes is widely considered Britain's national dish.

recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 200C / Gas 7. The high heat is needed to get the chips crispy.

content.text: The chips go in the oven first. While they bake, you make the batter and fry the fish. Timing them to finish together is the only tricky part.

items.prepNote: plus extra for dusting the fish

content.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Toss the chips with 2 tablespoons of oil and a good pinch of salt on a large baking tray. Spread in a single layer.
Bake the chips for 30 to 35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
When the chips have about 10 minutes left, make the batter: whisk the flour, milk, and a pinch of salt until smooth. It should be the consistency of thick double cream.
Pat the cod fillets dry. Dust lightly with extra flour, shaking off any excess.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Dip each fillet in the batter, let the excess drip off, and lay in the pan.
Fry for 4 minutes each side until golden and crisp. The fish is done when it flakes easily.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper. Serve with the chips, mushy peas, and vinegar.

items.cause: Fish was wet or not dusted with flour first.
items.fix: Pat fish very dry; dust with flour before dipping in batter.

items.cause: Oven not hot enough or chips were overcrowded.
items.fix: Use two trays if needed; keep chips in a single layer.
